text: Section 1. The maximum concentration of acetone in process water is 10 mg/L. Records shall be retained for 3 years.
Section 2. The maximum concentration of benzene in process water is 5 mg/L. Records shall be retained for 5 years.
Section 3. The maximum concentration of toluene in process water is 20 mg/L. Records shall be retained for 4 years.
Section 4. The maximum concentration of methanol in process water is 15 mg/L. Records shall be retained for 3 years.
Section 5. The maximum concentration of ethanol in process water is 25 mg/L. Records shall be retained for 2 years.
Section 6. The maximum concentration of xylene in process water is 8 mg/L. Records shall be retained for 5 years.
Section 7. The maximum concentration of ammonia in process water is 12 mg/L. Records shall be retained for 4 years.
Section 8. The maximum concentration of phenol in process water is 6 mg/L. Records shall be retained for 3 years.
Article 9. Operators must inspect the storage vessel every 12 months and retain the inspection report.
Article 10. Operators must inspect the transfer line every 6 months and retain the inspection report.
Article 11. Operators must inspect the pressure valve every 3 months and retain the inspection report.
Article 12. Operators must inspect the emergency pump every 6 months and retain the inspection report.
Table 1. Protective gloves are required when the exposure duration exceeds 30 minutes.
Table 2. Eye protection is required when the airborne concentration exceeds 2 ppm.
Table 3. Respiratory protection is required when ventilation is unavailable.
Table 4. Protective clothing is required when direct skin contact is possible.
